_comment: The message parity fixture (W7-R8). The report and the form word a finding in two runtimes that do not
read each other: the report renders php/messages/catalog.json through MessageCatalog, and js/engine.js
carries its own sentences. This file is what holds the two together.
Each case is one catalogue key: a rule in the shape the page hands the engine, a finding of that rule, and
the values a form would hold. For each audience it carries two sentences:
catalogue - for staff, the report's "What is wrong" cell (ScanColumns over a ScanDimensions built from
the rule, so the detail sentence comes as the panel and the CSV get it); for a survey,
MessageCatalog::explain() with the survey audience;
engine    - what the form shows for the same rule and values: the text of the field's message region,
without its status mark.
"parity" is "same" when the two are one sentence and "differs" when they are not.
tests/messages_fixture_php.php renders the catalogue side and tests/messages_fixture_js.cjs the engine
side. Both fail when a sentence changes and this file does not, and when a parity mark stops being true.
A case whose form is null is one the form never shows; formAbsent says why. Every catalogue key has a
case without a variant, and the PHP test fails for a key added to the catalogue without one. A variant
is the same key worded by the rule's own message.
Most sentences differ. The engine words a finding with the live values (the dates of the window, the
record that holds the value) and, for most checks, tells a respondent what it tells staff. The catalogue
words a finding for a table, and its survey line is shown on no page. Moving either side's wording is a
decision about the other side too, so change this file in the same commit.
